audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Graves Levels 1-3 and Neeko a shared 6 and first item; the packet flagged it outright ('level chart contradicts data'). It also contradicted the page's own whys[0] ('you edge the opening') and whys[4] ('even your Pop Blossom spike is contested').
audit.why: The mirror set both charts to Neeko / Skill / Graves / Graves / Graves / Graves / Skill with Graves-side ratings 4,5,7,7,7,7,5. My side must be the inverse of that, and it matches the why-text already written here.
audit.corrected: Row 0 -> Neeko 6/10, row 1 -> Skill 5/10, rows 2 and 3 stay Graves at 3/10, rows 4 and 5 -> Graves 3/10, row 6 -> Skill 5/10. One atomic group, all pairs proposed together.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 and first item were marked as Neeko-favourable stages while the text beneath them explains he dashes out of the root and kites the wind-up.
audit.why: Quickdraw is a dash whose cooldown drops every time he lands an auto, so the one window Neeko has is not reliable enough to own a stage. Graves' first item takes the side lane outright.
audit.corrected: Both rows moved to Graves; spike text left as the honest description of his threat window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Smoke Screen is described three times as blinding your autos. It does not blind — it creates a cloud that reduces sight range, and enemies hit by the initial impact take magic damage and are briefly slowed.
audit.why: Riot's text names sight reduction and a slow, with no blind anywhere. A player who thinks his W blinds will keep auto-attacking inside it expecting misses; what actually happens is he loses vision and gets kited. The mirror made the same correction from Graves' side.
audit.corrected: whys[3], late and wants.foe[1] now say sight range and slow.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three places tell the player to ult 'after W invis' / 'after Shapesplitter's invis'. Neeko has no invisibility.
audit.why: Riot's Shapesplitter text is a third-attack magic damage proc with a brief move speed gain, plus a directional clone. The concealment that exists is Inherent Glamour, and Riot explicitly states the Pop Blossom preparation is hidden while disguised — that is the mechanic the whole level 6 plan should rest on.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text, mid and wants.you[1] rebuilt on the disguise and the hidden preparation.

audit.whatIsWrong: Quickdraw is called the matchup clock but no cooldown was ever given, and the resist buff was written as generic 'armor stacks'.
audit.why: It is 16/15/14/13/12s, the buff is True Grit (armour and magic resist, doubled when he dashes toward a champion), and hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers the cooldown. That last clause is the reason a naive 'wait out the cooldown' plan fails.
audit.corrected: Real cooldown and the auto-refresh written into dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and mid.

edits.before: Without ult you can't all-in, and his kite-and-burst with E plus smoke-blinded autos out-trades your Blooming Burst poke.
edits.after: Without ult you can't all-in, and Quickdraw kiting plus Smoke Screen cutting your sight range out-trades your Blooming Burst poke.

edits.before: Pop Blossom unseen: ult while disguised as a teammate or after W invis, land E, then R-stun for a real all-in — your one clean kill threat before he out-tanks you.
edits.after: Pop Blossom unseen: disguised as a teammate the preparation is hidden, so land E then R-stun for a real all-in — your one clean kill threat before he out-tanks you.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are his — you can't all-in without ult and his shotgun + E kiting out-trades your poke, so farm with Q and chip only when his E is down. At 6 you get your one clean kill threat: set up Pop Blossom unseen, either ulting while disguised as a teammate or after Shapesplitter's invis, land Tangle-Barbs, then leap-stun before he can dash out. That's your window — but be honest, if he dodges the root or you ult on his E, he kites the channel and bursts you. Look to shove and roam with disguise pressure rather than forcing a coin-flip 1v1.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are his — you can't all-in without ult and his shotgun plus Quickdraw kiting out-trades your poke, so farm with Q and chip only when the dash is down. At 6 you get your one clean kill threat: set Pop Blossom up while disguised as a teammate so the preparation stays hidden, land Tangle-Barbs, then leap-stun before he can dash out. That's your window — but Quickdraw is 16s at rank 1 and every auto he lands shortens it, so count his hits. Shove and roam with disguise pressure rather than forcing a coin-flip 1v1.

edits.before: In a straight side lane Graves reclaims this — his lifesteal-into-tank ADC build outlasts your single Q+E+R rotation, he kites your short range, and smoke blinds your autos while his crits melt you with no escape once W and your shields are down. Your path to winning late is teamfights, not the 1v1: Liandry's plus your AoE Pop Blossom bomb deletes him if he's clustered with his team, and a landed E locks him for the rest of your combo. Group, don't duel — convert your 6-and-first-item pick pressure before the game becomes his scaling shotgun show.
edits.after: In a straight side lane Graves reclaims this — his lifesteal-into-tank build outlasts your single Q+E+R rotation, he kites your short range, and Smoke Screen cuts your vision and slows you while his crits melt a body with no escape once your clone is spent. Your path to winning late is teamfights, not the 1v1: Liandry's plus your AoE Pop Blossom bomb deletes him if he's clustered with his team, and a landed E locks him for the rest of your combo. Group, don't duel — convert your pick pressure before the game becomes his shotgun show.

edits.before: Hit Level 6 and set up Pop Blossom unseen via disguise or W invisibility so the stun lands before he can E out
edits.after: Hit Level 6 and set up Pop Blossom while disguised, so the hidden wind-up lands the stun before he can E out

edits.before: Kite at shotgun range, blind your autos with smoke (W), and burst your squishy body on his reload windows
edits.after: Kite at shotgun range, cut your sight with Smoke Screen (W), and burst your squishy body between reloads

edits.before: Dash + armor stacks — burst him after the charges are spent. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Quickdraw is 16s at rank 1, but every auto he lands cuts it — count his hits, then commit right after he burns it.

edits.before: Track Graves’s Quickdraw: Dash + armor stacks — burst him after the charges are spent. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Quickdraw: the dash grants True Grit resists, doubled if he dashes at you, and his autos shorten it. Step up once it is spent.

notes: Worth knowing: Graves' passive fires four bullets that cannot pass through units, so standing behind your own minion wave is a real damage reduction against his autos in a way it is not against most ADCs. That mechanic appears nowhere on this page and there was no string I could shorten to fit it without dropping something already true. It would make a strong addition to breakdown.wave or dosFull if the user wants it added outside the length band.
